name: France
summary_text: France is very safe for a transgender visitor, with risk concentrated on two specific situations. If you are arrested for any reason, including a protest or minor offence, a trans woman is likely to be placed in a men's prison on the basis of her legal gender — a systemic practice documented with foreign trans women (Argentine, Ecuadorian) subjected to genital-exam "verification," isolation and abuse. France's own detention watchdog says trans detainees "suffer the most," and a 2025 case (Louna, held in a men's prison in isolation) drew parliamentary censure. At the border , trans women — especially racialised or Latin-American travellers — have been humiliated by French border police (the documented Giovanna case at Paris CDG), and the airport waiting-zones draw repeated discrimination criticism. Offsetting this: there is no restriction on bathroom use, and the social norm leans trans-inclusive (a Lyon hostel in 2024 sanctioned a guest who complained about a trans person in a female dorm as "transphobic"). Anti-discrimination and hate-crime law cover gender identity. The risk is harassment-level in day-to-day tourism, with the serious-but-rare arrest/placement axis being the main caveat.

sources.title: The Plight Of Trans Women In Prison
sources.claim_summary: BuzzFeed News feature (Jan 2018): trans women in France incarcerated on the basis of their legal gender fall into a legal gray area and are punished beyond their alleged crimes - placement problems in the French prison system.

CGLPL opinion of 25 May 2021 on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty: based on ~40 referrals since 2010, finds serious violations of fundamental rights persist across all places of detention; recommendations also apply to intersex and non-binary persons.

Association for the Prevention of Torture blog: interview with the French NPM (CGLPL) on its 2021 opinion - trans persons deprived of liberty face constant risk of violence, discrimination and abuse; a new opinion was needed because the 2010 opinion had not resolved the problems.

sources.title: Autoroute A69 : Pourquoi Louna, femme transgenre, est détenue dans une prison pour hommes
sources.claim_summary: 20 Minutes (Feb 2025, in French): why Louna, a trans woman arrested in the A69 motorway protests, was detained in a men's prison - illustrates ongoing placement problems for trans women in French custody.

sources.title: Question n°219 : Condition des femmes transgenres en prison : le cas de Louna - Assemblée nationale
sources.claim_summary: French National Assembly oral question no. 219 (17th legislature) on the condition of transgender women - parliamentary scrutiny of the treatment of trans women (including in detention).

sources.title: Giovanna, femme transgenre, humiliée par la police en plein milieu de l’aéroport | StreetPress
sources.claim_summary: StreetPress first-person account (2017, in French): trans woman Giovanna Rincon describes being humiliated by border police at Roissy airport on returning from Colombia - 'delit de facies' as a daily nightmare for trans people; officers questioned her right to be in France despite 15 years' residence.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying InfoMigrants piece covers a report slamming France's border waiting zones as unequal, humiliating and discriminatory.

Women's Forum Australia (Aug 2024): an Australian traveller at a Lyon hostel was threatened with 'transphobia' charges by the manager after raising concerns about a man in the female-dorm bathroom - a contested incident reflecting gendered-space tensions in France. (Source has a sex-based-rights perspective.)

sources.title: Droits des personnes transgenres : la Défenseure des droits publie une nouvelle décision-cadre | Défenseur des Droits
sources.claim_summary: Défenseur des droits (French national rights ombudsman): new framework decision on the rights of transgender people - official findings and guidance on discrimination against trans people in France.

sources.title: Client Challenge
sources.claim_summary: Le Monde (Mar 2025): 'France updates US travel advice over gender "at birth"' — France's foreign ministry warns travellers to the United States that US authorities recognise only sex assigned at birth, so visas/ESTA and documents must match, and urges checking the US embassy site for new measures.

sources.title: French couple ties the knot in first same-sex wedding | CNN
sources.claim_summary: CNN (May 2013): report on France's first same-sex wedding, performed days after the marriage-equality law took effect.
